topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the lecture, framing how the session will explore the initiation and resolution of inflammation using previously introduced immune concepts.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the molecular signals of infection and cellular damage detected by the innate immune system and the general properties required for effective pathogen recognition.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and intracellular signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms, cellular localizations, and downstream signaling cascades of specific pattern recognition systems, focusing on toll-like receptors, cytosolic sensors, and inflammasomes.

topics.label: Cellular dynamics and physiological outcomes of acute inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the cellular and systemic cascade of acute inflammation triggered by activated tissue sentinels, from local leukocyte extravasation to whole-body physiological effects.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the post-inflammatory phases of immune responses, focusing on the mechanisms that shut down inflammation, rebuild tissue homeostasis, and manage persistent inflammatory stimuli.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
